cards.text: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus, is writing to Timothy, his true child in the faith (1 Timothy 1:1-2). He's just warned that the love of money is a root of all kinds of evil, and that some who crave it have wandered away from the faith (1 Timothy 6:10). Then he turns to Timothy: "But you, O man of God…" and friend, when a sentence starts with "But you," you sit up STRAIGHT.

cards.question: After warning about the love of money, Paul tells Timothy, the man of God, to ___ from these things.

cards.text: Flee means FLEE, not back away slowly while you're still staring at it. Then Paul hands Timothy a list: righteousness, godliness, faith, love, perseverance and gentleness.

cards.question: Righteousness, godliness, faith, love, perseverance and gentleness. What does Paul tell Timothy to do with that list?

cards.text: Then Paul says, "Fight the good fight of the faith." A FIGHT, friend, and here I am with nothing but a mustache, putting up my dukes anyway.

cards.question: Paul tells Timothy to take hold of the ___ life he was called to.

cards.text: Paul reminds Timothy when that call came: when he made the good confession.

cards.question: Timothy made his good confession in private, with no one else around.

cards.text: Then Paul gets SERIOUS and charges Timothy in the presence of God, who gives life to all things, and of Christ Jesus. Friend, this is not a "when you get a sec" kind of message.

cards.question: Paul says Christ Jesus made the good confession too. In His testimony before whom?

cards.text: That's Pontius Pilate, the governor (Matthew 27:2). And look at that: "the good confession" again, the same words Paul just used for Timothy.

cards.question: Paul charges Timothy to keep this commandment without stain or reproach. Until when?
Paul gives Timothy a date for when Jesus Christ will appear.

cards.text: Paul says the blessed and only Sovereign One, the King of kings and Lord of lords, will bring it about in His own time. Only the Father knows that day or hour (Matthew 24:36), and that's why I keep my ovens ready.
And Paul's not done. He says the Sovereign One alone is immortal and dwells in unapproachable light.

cards.question: Paul says no one has ever seen the Sovereign One.
After describing the Sovereign One like that, how does Paul wrap up this part of his letter?

cards.text: After his Amen, Paul circles back to money, with instructions for those who are rich in the present age. Friend, I came out of a clearance bin with a 25-cent sticker on me, but I'm listening anyway.

cards.question: Paul tells Timothy to instruct the rich not to be conceited, and not to put their hope in wealth, but in ___.
Paul describes wealth as something uncertain.

cards.text: And Paul says God richly provides all things for us to enjoy. Paul wrote ENJOY, friend, so if anybody asks why I'm grinning at a tray of chocolate chips, I've got backup.
Then Paul gives Timothy more to tell the rich. And he takes the word "rich" and flips it right around on them.

cards.question: Paul tells Timothy to instruct the rich to be rich in something besides money. What is it?
Paul also tells Timothy to instruct the rich to be generous and ready to ___.

cards.text: Paul tells them to do good, too. Giving money away sounds like watching it walk right out the door, but Paul says they're actually treasuring something up for themselves.

cards.question: When the rich are generous, what does Paul say they treasure up for themselves?

answers.text: A firm foundation for the future
A good name in the city

cards.text: All so that they may take hold of that which is truly life. There's "take hold" again, just like when Paul told Timothy to take hold of eternal life.
Then Paul writes, "O Timothy, guard what has been entrusted to you." Friend, that's somebody handing you their spare key and then looking you dead in the eyes.

cards.question: As he finishes his letter, what does Paul tell Timothy to avoid?
Paul says no one who professed so-called knowledge has swerved away from the faith.
Paul closes the whole letter with a short blessing for his readers. What does he say should be with them all?
